**Proposed mechanism:** DMD mutation (null) —DISRUPTS→ DMD (HGNC:2915); DMD (HGNC:2915) —DISRUPTS→ Dystrophin-glycoprotein complex (GO:0031270); Dystrophin-glycoprotein complex (GO:0031270) —DISRUPTS→ Sarcomere organization (GO:0030020); Sarcomere organization (GO:0030020) —DISRUPTS→ Muscle contraction (GO:0006939); Muscle contraction (GO:0006939) —LEADS_TO→ Duchenne muscular dystrophy (MONDO:0010679); Muscle contraction (GO:0006939) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial septal defect (HP:0001631). Loss-of-function mutations in the DMD gene disrupt the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex, which in turn disrupts sarcomere organization. Impaired sarcomere organization leads to defective muscle contraction, manifesting as both Duchenne muscular dystrophy in skeletal muscle and atrial septal defects in cardiac muscle due to the critical role of dystrophin in cardiac structure and function.

**How to falsify it:** If specific mutations in DMD are found to exclusively affect skeletal muscle without any discernible impact on cardiac muscle structure or function, or if genetic studies reveal distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways for cardiac defects in the context of DMD mutations compared to skeletal muscle defects. _(variant: Identification of common variants (gnoMAd AF > 1%) in the DMD gene that are strongly associated with atrial septal defects without any association with muscular dystrophy phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular mechanisms, particularly the disruption of sarcomere organization and muscle contraction due to DMD gene mutations, could lead to the development of therapies that target these common pathways to treat both skeletal and cardiac manifestations of muscular dystrophies, potentially improving cardiac outcomes in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
